title: All Source Analyst
tagline: With any mission, there are many moving parts and information coming from dozens (if not hundreds) of sources across the globe and stratosphere. The All-source Analyst’s duty is to discover, develop and dissect raw data, and assess viable intelligence across these various sources. They evaluate and ensure all intelligence activities are accurate and optimized to enable Space Force acquisitions, tests and operations.

ai.blurb: Pulls together intelligence from satellites, intercepts, people and public sources, then tells commanders what it means.
ai.dayToDay: Most of the work happens at a desk inside a secure facility, reading reports, cross-checking sources and writing assessments nobody outside the room will ever see. You'll work alongside other analysts and brief officers who want clear answers fast, often about adversary weapon systems and what they can do. Expect long stretches of careful reading punctuated by deadlines, and a fair amount of teaching others what to collect and how to report it.
ai.funFact: Goodfellow Air Force Base in San Angelo, Texas, is the military's main intelligence training hub, teaching students from all services — it's the common starting point for Space Force all-source analysts.

title: Cryptologic Analyst
tagline: Many of our country’s greatest threats reside in cyberspace as bad actors try to extract critical information invisible to the untrained eye. Cryptologic Analysts are expertly trained to identify, analyze and report on these complex problems to ensure intelligence operations are accurate, efficient and secure from outside threats. Their critical thinking is vital in deciphering time-sensitive information to support our global operations and key decision-makers.

You'll be on classified computer systems and specialised electronic equipment, picking apart signals intelligence and cyber data, then writing reports — some of which go to very senior people on short deadlines. It's a team environment, usually joint, with analysts from other services sitting nearby.

title: Cyber Operations
tagline: Our defense relies on cybersecurity across a multitude of advanced computers and softwares. Military satellites, missile guidance and ground combat — it’s all connected and must be secured from every angle possible. It’s our Cyber Operations specialist’s job to protect our cyber operations across four key specialties: defense, radio frequency and satellite communications, systems, and networks. They assess and report vulnerabilities, repair and install client systems, and protect our network infrastructure to ensure missions and communications run efficiently.

Responsible for analyzing imagery from satellites, remotely driven vehicles and more, Geospatial Intelligence specialists identify unusual activity and possible threats. They manage and perform a wide range of activities to exploit, develop and disseminate multi-sensor equipment to achieve commander objectives.

Prepare and present intelligence reports

Perform targeting support for development and combat assessment

It's patient, detail-heavy work done alongside other analysts, and the hardest part is usually noticing the small thing that changed.

title: Acquisition Manager
tagline: Facilitates the logistics needed to ensure a successful launch.
overview: The safety and success of our Guardians depend upon having what they need when they need it. And it’s up to Acquisition Managers to develop the structures and train their staff to make it all happen. From implementing engineering to securing final shipping, they oversee all aspects of the process to ensure the necessary equipment and supplies get where they need to be anywhere in the world.
duties: Manage and administer defense acquisition programs
Plan and develop program management techniques and training programs
Coordinate with commanders and staff to develop proper acquisition plans and schedules
Ensure quality assurance and support for all systems and equipment
requirements: Bachelor’s degree

ai.blurb: Runs the buying and delivery side of Space Force programs, making sure kit and systems arrive where they're needed.
ai.dayToDay: Mostly offices, meetings and spreadsheets rather than launch pads — you're managing programmes, schedules and contracts, and the people who work on them. You'll coordinate with commanders, engineers and contractors, chase quality assurance issues, and build training for your own staff. The pace is deadline-driven: programmes have milestones, and someone has to keep them honest.
ai.funFact: Defence acquisition is its own professional discipline in the US military, with a formal certification system — officers in this field spend careers learning contracting and programme management rather than operating equipment.
goodFitIf: You enjoy negotiating with engineers and contractors

title: Cyberspace Effects Operations Officer
tagline: Ensures the effectiveness of cyberspace operations, from planning missions to supervising satellite communications.
overview: With the constant evolution of today’s technology, information and communications can be optimized like never before. Responsible for a wide range of weaponry, training and intelligence efficiencies, Cyberspace Effects Operations Officers are the foremost experts on the vast world of cyberspace. From computerized, satellite and airborne communications to postal operations and tracking systems, these irreplaceable assets play a critical role in planning missions and ensuring the effectiveness of our cyberspace capabilities.
duties: Review mission tasking, intelligence, terrain and weather information
Operate weapons systems and command crew
Conduct or supervise training to ensure operational readiness of crewmembers
Advise commanders on associated risks and mitigation factors in conjunction with utilized technologies
Direct employment of cyberspace capabilities in both deliberate and crisis action scenarios
requirements: Bachelor’s degree with a focus in computer and information sciences, engineering, mathematics, computer science, management information systems or other related disciplines

ai.blurb: Plans and directs military cyberspace operations, commanding crews who run cyber weapons systems and satellite communications.

Pace swings between steady deliberate planning and sudden crisis-action tasking.
ai.funFact: The job's remit is broader than hacking: official duties stretch from satellite and airborne communications to tracking systems and even postal operations.

You can explain risk to non-experts
You stay calm under sudden tasking

title: Mechanical Engineer Officer
tagline: In order for us to complete our missions, our technology simply cannot fail. Covering a wide range of specialties ranging from astronautical and computer systems to flight test and mechanical, Mechanical Engineers provide advanced skills and knowledge of their particular specialties. Responsible for everything from the planning to implementation of their projects, these experts are essential to the success of operations all over the world.

duties: Plan, organize and implement systems engineering processes
Conduct design studies and manage studies contracted to industries
Coordinate engineering and technical management activities
Continuously analyze technical policies and procedures, products, and services to improve customer support
Identify and incorporate new technologies and subsystems
requirements: Bachelor’s degree in engineering related to one of the following specialties: aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, computer, electrical, electronics, communication or mechanical
Completion of the Defense Acquisition University
Fundamentals of Systems Acquisition Management course or Acquisition Fundamentals course
Completion of the Air Force Flight Test Engineer course or comparable
Minimum of 24 months of experience in qualified position or a master’s degree in a specified discipline and 12 months’ experience or a Doctor of Philosophy degree in a specified discipline
Completion of Officer Training School (OTS), Air Force Academy (USAFA) or Air Force Reserve Officer Training Corps (AFROTC)
Must be between the ages of 18 and 42

ai.blurb: Engineering officer who designs, tests and manages the hardware and systems Space Force missions depend on.
ai.dayToDay: Mostly office, lab and test-facility work rather than field work: design studies, systems engineering reviews, and managing contracts with aerospace companies building the kit. You spend a lot of time with contractors, programme managers and fellow engineers, chasing requirements, schedules and test results. The pace is project-driven, with quiet analytical stretches punctuated by deadlines and design reviews.
ai.funFact: A sizeable chunk of the job is acquisition work, which is why the training list includes Defense Acquisition University courses — much of military engineering is deciding what to buy and holding industry to its promises.
goodFitIf: you want technical work over field work
you're patient with paperwork and process

title: Space Operations Officer
tagline: Plans, organizes and directs space operations.
overview: The possibilities of enhancing our military effectiveness through the use of space are virtually endless. Space Operations Officers direct the entire system utilizing satellites that enhance our communication and tracking. They oversee space surveillance, spacelift, space warning and satellite command and control. By assessing the effectiveness of all space operations and incorporating new technology as it becomes available, they develop future plans for systems, facilities and personnel in order to defend our nation.
duties: Formulate space operations policies
Establish training requirements and performance standards for all systems
Coordinate space operations activities
Plan, organize and direct space operations programs
Provide guidance on proper use and care of sensitive materials
requirements: Any Bachelor or Master of Science degree
training: After training: | 115 | | ---------- | | days of Officer Training |

ai.blurb: Runs military satellite operations — command and control, space surveillance, launch support and missile warning.
ai.dayToDay: Most of the work happens in operations centres on the ground: consoles, screens, checklists and crews running satellite command and control, tracking objects in orbit, or supporting launches. As an officer you lead and supervise those crews rather than sit at a console all day, setting training standards, writing policy and coordinating with other units. Expect shift work in some assignments, plenty of briefings, and a security clearance.
ai.funFact: The Space Force is the smallest US military branch, and its members have been called Guardians since 2020 — a name borrowed from an old Air Force Space Command motto.
goodFitIf: You want to lead a crew
